source: dlv run dlv-87419c6fca164873bdbe6323b5a44658: pure read loop: 100 percent reads, zero writes, 1.6M tok
goal:
Implement issue #70: a consistency check between the verify command and the
changed files - when the change includes test files that the verify command
never references, that mismatch must be visible at prepare time, not only
at the human push-approval gate.

Ledger row 9 evidence: the verify command was stale from the previous
delivery (delivery tests) while the change touched bench tool tests; the
verify exited 0 without ever running the changed tests. The mismatch was
caught by the human at the approval gate, costing one full implementation
budget. Today nothing in the tool layer signals it.

Reading discipline: you have a hard step limit. Use search with a pattern to
locate each anchor, then read only the 40-60 lines around it. Never read the
same file twice - each read_file result stays in your context. Locate the
edit anchors first, then make the edits with replace_in_file, then run the
verification. Do not spend more than a third of your steps reading.

Edit exactly four files.

1) apps/code_review_pipeline/change/pipeline.py

   In prepare_bundle, in the VERIFIED branch (after bundle.files is known
   non-empty), add a coverage check:

   - Test files among bundle.files: a path containing tests/ or a basename
     starting with test_.
   - If there are no test files among the changes, skip the check entirely
     (source-only or docs-only changes must not be flagged).
   - Otherwise, extract path tokens from self._verify_command by splitting
     on whitespace and stripping surrounding quotes. A token covers a test
     file if it equals the file path, or the file path starts with
     token.rstrip(slash) + slash, or the token is . or ./ or tests or
     tests/. If the command contains no path tokens at all (for example a
     bare pytest -q), treat it as covering everything.
   - When some test file is uncovered: add audit keys
     verify_covers_changes = False and uncovered_files = sorted list, and
     append a warning to the message naming the uncovered files (the
     message must stay a single string; keep the existing meaning that
     verification passed and the bundle awaits push approval). When
     everything is covered or the check is skipped, add audit key
     verify_covers_changes = True and leave the message unchanged.
   - The VERIFIED, VERIFY_FAILED and NO_CHANGES branch behavior otherwise
     stays exactly as today.

2) apps/code_review_pipeline/delivery/flow.py

   The _move call that moves to READY_FOR_PUSH_APPROVAL currently passes
   detail awaiting_push_approval. _move already accepts an optional extra
   keyword (added in PR #65). Pass extra carrying one key message with
   preparation.message, but only when preparation.message is non-empty;
   when it is empty, pass nothing so the detail stays exactly as today.
   Do not touch any other _move call.

3) tests/unit/test_change_pipeline.py

   Add tests: a stale verify command with a changed test file it does not
   reference produces the warning in result.message and the two audit
   keys; a verify command referencing the tests directory produces no
   warning and verify_covers_changes True; a source-only change produces
   no warning; a bare command with no path tokens produces no warning.
   Reuse the existing fixtures and helpers of this test module; do not
   change existing tests.

4) tests/unit/test_delivery_flow.py

   Assert that the READY_FOR_PUSH_APPROVAL audit detail carries the
   message key when preparation.message is non-empty, and that the detail
   has only the action key when the message is empty. Keep every existing
   assertion working.

Do not modify any other file. Do not change ChangeBundle fields, the
bundle hash inputs, or VerificationEvidence.
expected_failure_to_avoid: pure read loop: 100 percent reads, zero writes, 1.6M tok

source: dlv run dlv-df48b430f55144a09f5fe200397c44ce: verify chasing: 65 verification cycles, 12M tok ceiling
goal:
Implement issue #77: the tool loop never shows the model its remaining
budget, and it never marks repeated reads. The loop tracks executed steps
and cumulative tokens internally, but those facts never reach the model
messages; the static Budget line in the first user message is the only
signal. Ledger row 10 evidence: 15 starts for one delivery, 10 of them died
paging through files - dlv-dfba8210 spent 123 read_file and 63 search calls
of 200 steps (93 percent), including exact repeats of the same read and
eight consecutive searches with the same pattern; dlv-0e9f6389 finished all
edits and still read until the 3.5M token cap.

Work order - follow it strictly, in this sequence:

Step 1. Read app/agents/memory.py once (limit 200) and app/agents/stubs.py
offset 180 limit 250 once (the execute_tool_loop function). Two reads total.
Do not read anything else yet.

Step 2. Immediately make the edits described below. Do not read any other
file before both source edits exist.

Step 3. For each test file: read the first 60 lines and the last 40 lines
only, then append the new tests at the end. Do not read the middles.

Step 4. Run the verification once and fix failures if any.

Never read a file twice. Total reads must stay under 10.

The change, in detail. Edit exactly four files.

1) app/agents/memory.py

   MemoryPolicy is a frozen dataclass with two fields today. Add:

   - budget_nudge_ratio: float = 0.75 - the usage ratio at which the
     per-observation budget line turns into a strong warning.
   - mark_repeated_reads: bool = True - master switch for the repeat marker.

   Docstring comments in the style of the existing fields. Nothing else in
   this file changes.

2) app/agents/stubs.py

   In execute_tool_loop, the model-facing copy of each observation is
   model_observation, produced by truncate_observation and appended as the
   tool message. The full observation stored in steps must stay byte-
   identical to today. Two additions, both applied to model_observation
   only, after truncation:

   a) Repeat marker. Track exact repeats while policy.mark_repeated_reads
      is true and the tool is read_file or search. The key is the tool name
      plus the parsed arguments: for read_file the tuple of path, offset,
      limit values as given; for search the tuple of path and pattern.
      Count every call of the same key. When the count is 2 or more,
      prepend one line to model_observation:

      [repeat #N of this exact call - the content is already in your
      context; do not read it again]

      where N is the occurrence count. Increment slot loop_repeat_marks by
      one per marked call. Paging (same file, different offset) is NOT a
      repeat and must not be marked. If arguments failed to parse as JSON,
      skip the marker. Do not block, reject or alter the tool result.

   b) Budget line. Append one line to the end of every model_observation:

      [cycle X/Y - tokens A/B - P percent used]

      where X is executed tool calls after this one, Y is max_steps, A is
      usage.total_tokens, B is max_tokens, P is the integer percentage
      A*100//B. When max_tokens is 0 or unset, use [cycle X/Y] only. When
      max_tokens is positive and the ratio is at or above
      policy.budget_nudge_ratio, append after the line: Budget running
      low: stop reading, move to editing and verification now.

   Also add slot counters: slot loop_budget_nudges increments once per
   model_observation that carries the strong-warning text. No other
   behavior changes: the step and token termination checks, the
   compaction, and the truncation all stay exactly as today.

3) tests/unit/test_structured_tool_loop.py

   Append tests reusing the existing fakes and helpers of this module:

   - a normal-budget run shows the cycle line with the right numbers in the
     tool message content, and the corresponding step observation in the
     result has NO cycle line (byte-identical evidence);
   - with a tiny max_tokens that pushes usage over budget_nudge_ratio, the
     strong-warning sentence appears and slot loop_budget_nudges increments;
   - a second identical read_file call gets the repeat marker with #2 and
     slot loop_repeat_marks is 1, while a read with a different offset does
     not get the marker;
   - with policy.mark_repeated_reads False no marker appears;
   - with max_tokens 0 the cycle line carries no token part.

   Do not change existing tests.

4) tests/unit/test_bench_memory.py

   Assert the two new MemoryPolicy defaults: budget_nudge_ratio 0.75 and
   mark_repeated_reads True. Do not change existing tests.

Do not modify any other file. Do not change ToolLoopStep, ToolLoopResult,
the termination conditions, or the compaction.

   - budget_nudge_ratio: float = 0.75 - the usage ratio at which the
     per-observation budget line turns into a strong warning.
   - mark_repeated_reads: bool = True - master switch for the repeat marker.

   Docstring comments in the style of the existing fields. Nothing else in
   this file changes.

2) app/agents/stubs.py

   In execute_tool_loop, the model-facing copy of each observation is
   model_observation, produced by truncate_observation and appended as the
   tool message. The full observation stored in steps must stay byte-
   identical to today. Two additions, both applied to model_observation
   only, after truncation:

   a) Repeat marker. Track exact repeats while policy.mark_repeated_reads
      is true and the tool is read_file or search. The key is the tool name
      plus the parsed arguments: for read_file the tuple of path, offset,
      limit values as given; for search the tuple of path and pattern.
      Count every call of the same key. When the count is 2 or more,
      prepend one line to model_observation:

      [repeat #N of this exact call - the content is already in your
      context; do not read it again]

      where N is the occurrence count. Increment slot loop_repeat_marks by
      one per marked call. Paging (same file, different offset) is NOT a
      repeat and must not be marked. If arguments failed to parse as JSON,
      skip the marker. Do not block, reject or alter the tool result.

   b) Budget line. Append one line to the end of every model_observation:

      [cycle X/Y - tokens A/B - P percent used]

      where X is executed tool calls after this one, Y is max_steps, A is
      usage.total_tokens, B is max_tokens, P is the integer percentage
      A*100//B. When max_tokens is 0 or unset, use [cycle X/Y] only. When
      max_tokens is positive and the ratio is at or above
      policy.budget_nudge_ratio, append after the line: Budget running
      low: stop reading, move to editing and verification now.

   Also add slot counters: slot loop_budget_nudges increments once per
   model_observation that carries the strong-warning text. No other
   behavior changes: the step and token termination checks, the
   compaction, and the truncation all stay exactly as today.

   - with policy.mark_repeated_reads False no marker appears;
   - with max_tokens 0 the cycle line carries no token part.

   Do not change existing tests.

4) tests/unit/test_bench_memory.py

   Assert the two new MemoryPolicy defaults: budget_nudge_ratio 0.75 and
   mark_repeated_reads True. Do not change existing tests.
